articles.title: Chrome V8 Zero-Day Exploited in the Wild Enables Code Execution Inside Sandbox
articles.summary: Google released patches for 230 security vulnerabilities in Chrome, including a medium-severity zero-day flaw in the V8 JavaScript engine that attackers are actively exploiting. The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write bug that allows code execution within Chrome's sandbox environment. This flaw demonstrates how even browser security layers can be compromised through engine-level bugs. Users should update Chrome immediately to protect against active attacks.
articles.whyItMatters: Active exploitation of this vulnerability means attackers are currently using it in real-world attacks, making immediate patching essential for all Chrome users. The ability to execute code inside Chrome's sandbox bypasses a critical security boundary, potentially allowing attackers to escape browser isolation and access system resources. articles.title: New cPanel Flaw Lets a Hosting Account With Mail Privileges Run Code as Root
articles.summary: cPanel released a security patch for a critical vulnerability affecting all supported versions of its software. The flaw allows hosting account users with mail privileges to upload arbitrary files through the EmailTrack feature and execute code with root-level permissions, giving them complete control over the server. This means a single compromised or malicious hosting account could potentially take over an entire server and all accounts hosted on it.
articles.whyItMatters: This vulnerability is critical because it affects a widely-used hosting control panel and allows authenticated users to escalate privileges to root level, potentially compromising all hosted websites and data on a shared server. Organizations using cPanel must apply the patch immediately to prevent attackers from gaining complete server control through mail-enabled hosting accounts.

articles.title: F5 BIG-IP APM Malware Injects a PHP Web Shell Into Memory, Evading Disk Scans
articles.summary: Malware targeting F5 BIG-IP Access Policy Manager devices uses a sophisticated technique to hide a PHP web shell in memory rather than on disk, allowing it to evade traditional security scans. When Apache processes the appliance's own PHP scripts, the malware injects the shell into the running memory copy, leaving the actual files untouched and appearing clean. This memory-based hiding method makes detection significantly harder for administrators relying on disk-based file integrity checks.
articles.whyItMatters: This attack demonstrates advanced evasion techniques that bypass standard disk-based security scans, making it harder for defenders to detect compromised systems. F5 BIG-IP APM devices are critical network infrastructure components, so their compromise poses a serious risk to organizational security. articles.title: Researcher Drops New Microsoft Defender PoC Showing ShieldBreak Patch Can Be Bypassed
articles.summary: A security researcher named Chaotic Eclipse has released a proof-of-concept exploit for a new vulnerability in Microsoft Defender called ShieldCrash, which bypasses the patch for a previously reported flaw (CVE-2026-69414, rated 7.8 CVSS). This indicates that Microsoft's initial fix for the ShieldBreak vulnerability was incomplete, leaving systems still exposed to attack. The disclosure highlights ongoing security gaps in one of the world's most widely used antivirus solutions.
articles.whyItMatters: Microsoft Defender protects millions of devices globally, so a bypass that circumvents its security patches represents a widespread and urgent threat. articles.title: SAP Patches CVSS 10.0 Kernel Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
articles.summary: SAP has released security patches for a critical vulnerability in SAP Extended Passport (EPP) Processing that allows attackers to execute code remotely without authentication. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-44756 with a perfect CVSS score of 10.0, stems from memory corruption issues and poses severe risks to system confidentiality, integrity, and availability. This is one of the most dangerous types of vulnerabilities because it requires no user interaction or credentials to exploit.
articles.whyItMatters: A CVSS 10.0 vulnerability with unauthenticated remote code execution capability represents an existential threat to any organization running affected SAP systems. Organizations must prioritize patching immediately, as this vulnerability likely requires no special access or user interaction, making it trivial for attackers to exploit at scale. articles.title: New Microsoft Defender 'ShieldCrash' zero-day grants SYSTEM access

The flaw represents a critical weakness in one of the world's most widely used security tools.

articles.title: Liquid Hackers Return 3,400 Bitcoin Taken via Elements Bug, Still Holding $47M in BTC
articles.summary: A hacker exploited a bug in the Liquid Network, a Bitcoin sidechain, to steal nearly 4,000 bitcoin on September 6, 2026. The Liquid Network remains paused, preventing users from converting their L-BTC tokens back into actual bitcoin.

articles.title: Autonomous AI Agents Compromise Thousands of Credentials in Under Six Hours

articles.title: WeChat Zero-Click Worm Took Over Accounts on iPhone and Android via Incoming Calls
articles.summary: Security researchers at Calif discovered a zero-click worm affecting WeChat that can hijack user accounts through incoming calls on both iPhone and Android devices. articles.summary: Attackers have successfully compromised F5 BIG-IP APM devices by deploying a sophisticated Linux rootkit that can inject malicious code directly into system memory. articles.whyItMatters: F5 BIG-IP APM devices are critical infrastructure components that manage application access and security for many organizations; a successful compromise could grant attackers persistent access to entire networks. articles.title: Microsoft releases Windows 10 KB5122878 extended security update

Users running Windows 10 are encouraged to install this update to protect their systems from known exploits.
articles.whyItMatters: Regular patching is critical for maintaining system security, as vulnerabilities left unpatched are actively exploited by attackers. This extended security update for Windows 10 provides essential protections that help prevent unauthorized access, malware infections, and data compromise. Delaying or skipping patches significantly increases organizational risk exposure.

articles.title: ShinyHunters hackers claim breach of Florida "DAVID" DMV database

articles.title: BengalSEO Poisons Bing Search Results to Deliver MayaBot and Tech Support Scams

articles.title: Grindr to Pay £26 Million to Settle U.K. Claims Over HIV Status Data Sharing
articles.summary: Grindr, a major LGBTQ+ dating application, has agreed to pay £26 million to resolve a U.K. lawsuit over improper sharing of sensitive user data with third parties. articles.title: Telerik UI Padding-Oracle Bug Chained to Unauthenticated RCE — Public Exploit Released
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered a critical vulnerability chain in Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX that exploits a padding-oracle weakness in AES-CBC encryption to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. articles.whyItMatters: This demonstrates how cryptographic implementation flaws can be chained into complete system compromise, even without authentication. articles.title: Two Alleged ‘TeamPCP’ Hackers Arrested in Australia

articles.title: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty in Snowflake Extortions

articles.title: Read This Before You Buy That TV Streaming Stick
articles.summary: Cheap TV streaming devices that promise unlimited content for a one-time fee pose serious security risks beyond what was previously known. These devices not only secretly rent out users' internet connections to strangers, but also impersonate mobile phones to fraudulently click ads on fake websites and deceive online merchants and advertising networks. Consumers should be cautious when purchasing budget streaming hardware, as the financial gains from these scams far outweigh the device's cost.
articles.whyItMatters: This highlights how consumer IoT devices can become vectors for multiple coordinated scams that harm both end-users and legitimate businesses. articles.whyItMatters: PEEP demonstrates how attackers can weaponize widely-used browsers as persistence mechanisms after gaining initial system access, making it extremely difficult for users and defenders to detect malicious activity hidden within trusted applications. articles.title: Google Releases Chrome Update to Patch Actively Exploited V8 Zero-Day
articles.summary: Google released a Chrome security update addressing 12 vulnerabilities, including a high-severity zero-day bug in V8 (the JavaScript engine) that attackers are already exploiting in the wild. The flaw, identified as CVE-2026-85046 with a CVSS score of 8.8, involves a type confusion error that could allow remote attackers to compromise systems. Users should update to Chrome version 152.0.7977.82 or later to protect themselves from active attacks.
articles.whyItMatters: Active exploitation means attackers are weaponizing this vulnerability right now, making immediate patching essential for all Chrome users. A high CVSS score combined with active exploitation in the wild creates urgent risk for data theft and system compromise. Delaying the update exposes your browser and system to real, present-day attacks.

articles.title: ChatGPT can now connect to your personal apps to mimic writing style
articles.summary: OpenAI is testing a new feature for ChatGPT that learns your personal writing style by accessing examples from your connected apps and accounts. This capability could make AI-generated content more personalized but raises concerns about how personal data is being collected and stored. Users should be aware of what information they're sharing with the platform when enabling this feature.
articles.whyItMatters: As AI tools gain access to personal data across multiple connected applications, understanding the privacy implications becomes critical for users. Organizations and individuals need to carefully evaluate what personal information they permit AI systems to analyze and retain, as this data could be vulnerable to misuse or breaches.

articles.title: Hackers exploit new MikroTik RouterOS flaws to hijack routers
articles.summary: Cybercriminals are actively exploiting two newly discovered security flaws in MikroTik RouterOS to gain unauthorized control of routers that have SSH access available online. By chaining these vulnerabilities together, attackers can compromise routers and potentially use them as entry points into networks or for other malicious activities. This threat is particularly dangerous because many organizations expose their routers directly to the internet.
articles.whyItMatters: Router compromises are critical infrastructure threats that can expose entire networks to attackers, enable data interception, and serve as launching points for further attacks. The active exploitation of chained vulnerabilities means this is an immediate threat requiring urgent patching for any organization running MikroTik RouterOS with internet-exposed SSH services.

articles.title: ConnectWise warns of new ScreenConnect flaw without patch
articles.summary: ConnectWise has identified a new security vulnerability in its ScreenConnect Remote Access software and is working on a patch expected later this week. In the meantime, the company has released temporary workarounds to help users protect their systems from potential exploitation. This vulnerability affects remote access capabilities that many businesses rely on for IT support and troubleshooting.
articles.whyItMatters: ScreenConnect is widely used by IT professionals and managed service providers for remote support, making this vulnerability a significant risk to business operations and customer systems. articles.title: N-able patches max severity N-central flaw amid ongoing attacks
articles.summary: N-able released an emergency patch for a critical remote code execution vulnerability in its N-central remote monitoring and management platform. The flaw has a maximum severity rating and is currently being exploited in active attacks. This urgent fix addresses a serious security gap that could allow attackers to gain unauthorized control over systems managed through the platform.
articles.whyItMatters: RMM platforms like N-central are trusted tools that manage thousands of client systems, making them high-value targets for attackers. An unpatched RCE vulnerability in such infrastructure can lead to widespread compromise across multiple organizations and their networks. The active exploitation confirms this is an immediate threat requiring urgent patching across all affected deployments.

articles.title: ChatGPT Astra is now rolling out to $20 Plus subscription
articles.summary: OpenAI has started rolling out ChatGPT Astra, its most advanced AI model, exclusively to users with $20 Plus subscriptions. Free users do not yet have access to this powerful new model. The rollout represents a significant upgrade in AI capabilities for paid subscribers.
articles.whyItMatters: As AI models become more powerful and widely deployed, understanding access controls and deployment strategies helps organizations assess AI security risks and plan adoption strategies. This rollout highlights how advanced AI capabilities are being distributed and the potential security implications of tiered access to powerful language models.
